analysis_state.reason: Stage 01 reproduced the AddressSanitizer wild-address read in `tcg_constant_folding_aarch64`. The exact staged source closes the witness copy into guest memory, the live-translation reachability, the AArch64 instruction fetch, the decode-family selection inside `disas_a64_insn()`, and the optimizer-side missing `args[i] < TCG_MAX_TEMPS` guard. What remains unresolved is the source-level translator write that stored the out-of-range temp id into the TCG operand stream later read as `args[i]` at `qemu/tcg/optimize.c:574`. `run_flags.json` disables runtime disambiguation and `trace_feedback.json` does not request the bounded exception, so Stage 02 must leave that producer explicit as unresolved instead of guessing a `disas_*` arm or `gen_opparam_buf` slot.

bug_description.normalized: The staged 60-byte `poc` is copied into Unicorn guest memory at 0x1000000 by `uc_mem_write()` and then executed by `fuzz_emu_arm64_arm`. Because there is no cached translation block for that PC, `tb_find_slow()` forces live AArch64 translation. `disas_a64_insn()` fetches attacker-controlled 32-bit instruction words from the guest-memory buffer and dispatches each word into one decoder family based on `extract32(insn, 25, 4)`. The saved AddressSanitizer trace proves that by the time `tcg_gen_code_common()` hands the translated operand array to `tcg_optimize()`, at least one input operand is already outside the valid temp-id range, and `tcg_constant_folding()` dereferences `temps[args[i]]` without first checking `args[i] < TCG_MAX_TEMPS`, producing the reproduced `SEGV` / `wild-addr-read` at `qemu/tcg/optimize.c:574`. The staged artifacts do not record which exact translator-side `disas_*` helper or `*gen_opparam_ptr++` write created that out-of-range operand, so this GT keeps the translator-to-optimizer bridge explicitly partial instead of claiming a closed per-slot data flow. The staged fix confirms the missing obligation by inserting `if (args[i] >= TCG_MAX_TEMPS) return NULL;` in `tcg_constant_folding()` and propagating the failed optimization back out of `tcg_gen_code_common()` / `tb_find_slow()` so translation aborts instead of dereferencing the invalid temp slot.

source.description: First project-side materialization of the witness into Unicorn guest-memory state: `uc_mem_write()` copies the attacker-controlled bytes into the mapped emulation buffer at the target address.
source.value_from: The harness passes `Data, Size` to `uc_mem_write()` after mapping 4 MB at 0x1000000. Inside `uc_mem_write()`, those fuzz bytes are aliased as `bytes` and copied into Unicorn's guest memory object state by `uc->write_mem()`.

tainted_value_origin.description: The first concrete translator value derived from the attacker-controlled guest buffer is the fetched 32-bit instruction word `insn`. The staged artifacts do not identify which later translator statement converted one witness instruction into the specific out-of-range optimizer operand.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: Reads 4-byte little-endian instruction words from the guest-memory bytes previously copied by `uc_mem_write()` at the current PC.
tainted_value_origin.note: This is intentionally narrower than the old `gen_opparam_buf` claim: Stage 02 can prove instruction fetch from attacker-controlled guest memory, but not the exact `disas_*` emit site of the bad `args[i]`.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer crash site. Copy propagation uses the malformed input operand as a direct index into `s->temps2` and reads from a wild address.
sink.note: The saved Stage 01 ASan trace reports `AddressSanitizer: SEGV` / `wild-addr-read` at `qemu/tcg/optimize.c:574:32` in `tcg_constant_folding_aarch64`.

root_cause.code: for (i = nb_oargs; i < nb_oargs + nb_iargs; i++) {
root_cause.description: The copy-propagation loop assumes every input operand is a valid temp id and reaches the next-line `temps[args[i]]` dereference without validating `args[i] < TCG_MAX_TEMPS`.
root_cause.note: The staged fix inserts `if (args[i] >= TCG_MAX_TEMPS) return NULL;` immediately inside this loop before the `temps[args[i]]` access, confirming the missing bounds check on optimizer input operands.

parser_admitted.description: At emulation start there is no cached translation block for guest PC 0x1000000, so Unicorn must translate the attacker-controlled guest buffer and enters the vulnerable optimization path instead of reusing an existing TB.

evidence_limitations: The saved ASan stack and staged vulnerable source prove that `tcg_constant_folding()` read an out-of-range `args[i]` from the translated TCG operand buffer, but they do not include a TCG op dump or marker identifying which exact AArch64 translator helper emitted that operand.

`run_flags.json` sets `runtime_disambiguation` to `false`, so Stage 02 did not instrument the translation path to resolve the specific `disas_*` arm or `gen_opparam_buf` write that produced the bad temp id.

The staged fix diff is source-relevant on the optimizer side: it adds the missing temp-range guard and propagates a NULL optimization result back out of code generation, but it still does not identify the vulnerable-build translator statement that emitted the bad temp id.

Local Unicorn history contains several later ARM/NEON commits whose messages also mention OSS-Fuzz issue 20079, but the staged witness and saved crash trace do not uniquely tie this sample to any one of those later source-side diffs. This GT therefore leaves the translator-side bad-operand emission as unresolved evidence rather than attributing it speculatively.

coarse_trace.summary: The harness maps guest memory at 0x1000000, passes the raw 60-byte witness into `uc_mem_write()`, and then starts AArch64 emulation from that buffer.
`uc_mem_write()` copies the witness bytes into Unicorn's guest-memory object state, creating the attacker-controlled code buffer later fetched by translation.
Because there is no cached translation block for the starting PC, Unicorn calls `tb_gen_code()` and enters live translation of the attacker-controlled guest buffer.

The AArch64 translator fetches witness instruction words and dispatches each one into an A64 decode family, but the staged artifacts do not identify which concrete `disas_*` helper appended the later out-of-range temp id to the translated operand stream.

`tcg_gen_code_common()` passes the translated operand array into `tcg_optimize()`, where `tcg_constant_folding()` trusts each input `args[i]` as an in-range temp id; the missing `args[i] < TCG_MAX_TEMPS` guard lets the malformed operand trigger the reproduced wild read.

fine_trace.code:
len = (size_t)MIN(size - count, mr->end - address);
if (uc->write_mem(&uc->as, address, bytes, len) == false)
fine_trace.note: Source. After the mapped region is accepted, `uc_mem_write()` computes the current chunk length and copies that slice of the staged witness from `bytes` into Unicorn guest memory at `address`. This is the first project statement that materializes the attacker-controlled guest code buffer used later by translation.

The AArch64 translator fetches the next 32-bit little-endian instruction word from the guest-memory bytes at the current PC. This is the last concrete value the staged artifacts tie directly to attacker-controlled data before the unresolved translator-side bad-operand emission.

The translator consumes the fetched instruction's top-level encoding bits to choose one A64 decode family. Those decode helpers are what emit the translated TCG ops and operand ids, but the staged artifacts do not preserve which specific `case` / `disas_*` arm produced the out-of-range temp id later observed in `args[i]`.

This is the first concrete optimizer entry point on the crashing path. `tcg_gen_code_common()` hands the translated operand array to `tcg_optimize()`, whose `args` parameter aliases `s->gen_opparam_buf`; the saved crash proves that at least one input slot is already out of range here, but the exact earlier translator-side `*gen_opparam_ptr++` write into that slot is not identified in the staged artifacts.

fine_trace.code: for (i = nb_oargs; i < nb_oargs + nb_iargs; i++) {
fine_trace.note: Root cause. Copy propagation walks the optimizer input array supplied at step 4 and assumes every `args[i]` is a valid temp id. The vulnerable loop performs no `args[i] < TCG_MAX_TEMPS` check before the next line dereferences `temps[args[i]]`.

Sink. When one translated input operand exceeds the temp-table range, `temps[args[i]].state` indexes `s->temps2` out of bounds and reproduces the saved AddressSanitizer `SEGV` / `wild-addr-read` at `qemu/tcg/optimize.c:574:32`.

cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: Partially. The saved ASan stack exactly matches the runtime suffix `tb_find_slow_aarch64 -> tb_gen_code_aarch64 -> cpu_arm_gen_code_aarch64 -> tcg_gen_code_common_aarch64 -> tcg_constant_folding_aarch64`. The unresolved part is the earlier translator-side write that placed the out-of-range temp id into the operand stream before `tcg_optimize()`.
cross_validation.tainted_value_reaches_sink: Partially. The staged source grounds the witness through guest-memory copy, AArch64 instruction fetch, decode-family selection, and optimizer entry, but it does not identify the exact translator-side `*gen_opparam_ptr++` write that populated the crashing `args[i]` slot.

format.contract: Exactly the 60-byte witness stored in `gt_results/arvo_20079/poc`, copied verbatim into guest memory at 0x1000000 by `uc_mem_write()`. Stage 01 reproduced the saved crash from this exact byte sequence under `fuzz_emu_arm64_arm`; no shorter prefix or broader instruction class was validated in Stage 02. The first 12 bytes are `10 EF EF 10 50 10 58 D5 ED BE 20 1E`.
